body.x: The Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that it opened the “Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion” at CES 2026, the Consumer Electronics Show, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States, and that it is presenting Incheon’s urban strategy to visitors from around the world.

The Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion occupies 139 square meters in the AI Zone of the North Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center and introduces the direction of urban innovation on the global stage by placing Incheon’s “AI City” vision at the forefront.

Under the theme “Destination Incheon — From Smart City to AI City,” the pavilion presents a comprehensive vision of a sustainable future city by showcasing AI-based urban services and innovation models applied across urban life, industry, and culture. The exhibition highlights residential environments that advance citizen services such as mobility, safety, energy, and health; workplaces that innovate across industrial sectors, including manufacturing, logistics, food, and pharmaceuticals; and creative urban spaces that generate content and experiences.

Key programs included the “Global AI City Forum,” which brought together global urban and industry experts to share Incheon’s next-generation AI city strategy and directions for cooperation. In particular, an exchange session with Fairfax County, Virginia, built on the economic development cooperation between the two sides and explored ways to expand collaboration in areas such as innovation ecosystem development, startup support, and technology demonstration.

Alongside pavilion operations, the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority rolled out programs focused on global networking and generating tangible cooperation outcomes. On the evening of January 7, the “Incheon Night at CES 2026” program facilitated partnership discussions and networking among participating Incheon companies, overseas companies, and stakeholders. On January 8, the authority operated an intensive business day for visiting delegations, conducting one-on-one business meetings, and on-site business matching with buyers and investors.

Incheon Mayor Yoo Jeong-bok said, “CES 2026 serves as an important stage to present to the world Incheon’s vision of leaping from a future growth city that has led Korea’s transformation and innovation for more than 20 years into an AI City,” adding, “We will continue to do our utmost to ensure that Incheon establishes itself as a leading global AI city.”
Information on participating companies at CES 2026 and programs at the Incheon–IFEZ Pavilion is available on the official website.

The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
